description: §40.8 + §4.12 (S445, ruling option b) — a plain `<program>` followed by a `<div>`-wrapped `<program auth="required">` is TWO top-level programs in one file (neither has a `<program>` or `<page>` ancestor), so E-PROGRAM-002 fires exactly once, on the second. Before S445 the E-PROGRAM-002 count read only the file's direct nodes: this compiled with 0 errors and the wrapped program's server functions answered anonymous callers (g-wrapped-program-auth-silently-dropped).
rationale: §40.8: 'A second (or later) top-level `<program>` in the SAME file SHALL be `E-PROGRAM-002`.' §4.12 (S445): a `<program>` is top-level when it has no `<program>` or `<page>` ancestor, whatever markup wraps it; both detectors read that one definition.
